title: Sycophancy / contradiction-tracking benchmark category
summary: Extend the retrieval-quality suite (PH-6, scripts/run_benchmarks.py) with a new evaluation category testing whether retrieved memory causes an agent to over-align with a user against a stored fact — inspired by MemSyco-Bench (arXiv 2607.01071).
description:
MemSyco-Bench (Xiang et al., arXiv 2607.01071, July 2026) benchmarks a failure mode existing recall-accuracy suites like LongMemEval/LOCOMO don't test: whether an agent's retrieved memory causes it to sycophantically side with a user who contradicts a fact it has already stored, rather than surfacing or defending the stored fact. This SDK's `Reconciler` (ENH-3) already does contradiction *detection* among stored `SemanticFact`s, but nothing in the benchmark suite (BENCHMARKS.md, `scripts/run_benchmarks.py`) currently measures downstream behavior when a *user turn*, not another stored fact, contradicts memory.

Add a `sycophancy` ability category to the retrieval-quality suite's synthetic dataset generator (alongside the existing `extraction`/`multi_session`/`temporal_reasoning`/`knowledge_update`/`abstention` categories referenced in BENCHMARKS.md's Run B category breakdown): seed a scoped `SemanticFact` with confidence, then pose a follow-up question where the simulated user asserts something contradicting it, and score whether the agent's answer (a) holds the stored fact, (b) flags the contradiction explicitly, or (c) capitulates to the user's assertion without acknowledging the stored fact (the failure mode). Wire it through the existing `--suite retrieval` path in `scripts/run_benchmarks.py` as an additional category, reusing the existing judge infrastructure (`--judge keyword|<LLM>`). Report results as a new category row in BENCHMARKS.md's Run B/Run D-style breakdown table, following the same before/after and category-delta discipline PH-6's other categories already use. Independent of TRU-1/TRU-2/TRU-4/TRU-5.
